brief:
An Israeli Arab left-wing party leader withdrew from the country's election after the Supreme Court signaled a majority of judges backed his disqualification, according to Al-Monitor. The court's advisory effectively gave him a choice between voluntary withdrawal and formal removal from the ballot.

The move reflected ongoing legal and political tensions surrounding Arab participation in Israeli elections, though specific details about the party leader's identity and the court's stated reasoning were not provided.
dek: By Pesha Magid JERUSALEM, Oct 2 (Reuters) - The head of a left-wing Arab party has dropped out of Israel's election after the country's Supreme Court advised him that a majority of judges supported disqualifying him if he did not voluntarily withdraw.
title: Israeli court pressure forces Arab party leader from election race
